name: Plastic Forming Inc
old_description: Considering placing an order? Visit us and come see how we get it done!
about:
Plastic Forming Inc. operates from Richland Hills, Texas, in the Fort Worth metro area. The company was founded in 1978 by Tom Stepp, a native Texan who spent over 20 years at Bell Helicopter before renting 2,500 square feet of industrial space with a single machine and two employees—one of them his wife, Dorothy, who handled bookkeeping. Their first projects included a children's swimming pool protector and a point-of-purchase display.

Today the firm occupies more than 45,000 square feet of manufacturing space and offers vacuum pressure forming (thermoforming), precision die-cutting, plastic fabricating, and packaging services. The thermoforming process heats plastic sheets and shapes them with vacuum or hydraulic pressure; molds are built in-house to customer specifications. Die-cutting handles materials such as paper, fabric, or thin metal for tight-tolerance components. Fabricating covers molding, machining, and forming of raw plastic into finished parts.

The company serves industries including automotive, electronics, packaging, and consumer goods, producing items such as disposable containers, custom packaging, and specialized components. Customers range from businesses needing short-run prototypes to those requiring ongoing production of formed plastic parts.

Stepp's founding values—transparency, integrity, and diligence—remain central to the operation. The company emphasizes a 5S workplace organization system to maintain efficiency and consistency, and its stated mission is to exceed expectations through innovation, quality, and sustainable practices.

name: Plastic Mold Technology Molding Facility

about:
Plastic Mold Technology operates from Kentwood, Michigan. The company traces its roots to 1958 when Adrian Woldring founded Woldring and Associates as an electrical discharge machining (EDM) sales business. By the late 1960s the firm had shifted to building plastic injection molds, primarily for the automotive sector. After Woldring's retirement in 1974, Gary Proos took on joint ownership and acquired the company outright in 1984.

Today the shop provides prototype and production tooling for a broad spectrum of injection molding processes. Its capabilities include standard injection molding, insert molding, second-shot overmolding, glass encapsulation, stack molds, gas assist, two-shot molding, rotary molding, and reaction injection molding (RIM). The facility handles both prototype and high-volume production tooling, though specific facility size, headcount, and annual volume are not disclosed.

The company's customer base centers on the automotive industry, where it has supplied molds for decades. It also serves other sectors requiring complex multi-material or multi-component tooling, though no additional industries are named in its public materials.

Plastic Mold Technology emphasizes the deep experience of its management and shop-floor personnel as a key differentiator, positioning that institutional knowledge as the foundation for delivering complex tooling solutions.

name: Plastic Molding Development
old_description: Plastic Molding Development was founded in Sterling Heights, Michigan in 1985. Today, it provides resources for automobile manufacturers around the globe.
about:
Plastic Molding Development was founded in 1985 in Sterling Heights, Michigan. The company began as a plastic injection molding resource and has since grown to serve automobile manufacturers worldwide.

The company operates a 35,000-square-foot facility equipped with a range of Van Dorn and Wittmann Battenfeld injection molding machines from 170 to 3,300 tons, supported by 10- to 40-ton cranes. Its core services include plastic injection molding, tool and mold testing, injection tryout testing, and short-run production, with capability for both steel and aluminum tooling.

Roughly 90 percent of its work serves the automotive industry, supporting OEMs, Tier 1 suppliers, and tool shops. The company also produces industrial and consumer products, as well as specialty and prototype parts for engineers and program managers.

Plastic Molding Development emphasizes its customer service, hospitality, and welcoming environment as key differentiators, alongside a commitment to safe, high-quality machinery and staying current with molding industry trends. The company also highlights fast turnaround for custom plastic molding development.

name: Plastic Molding Manufacturing, Berlin CT
old_description: Contact us today to find out how we can help with your industry or upcoming project. We have handled thousands of projects since 1968 and we are here to save you money or help solve your problems.
about:
Plastic Molding Manufacturing is headquartered in Berlin, Connecticut, and traces its origins to 1968 when founder George E. Danis established Danis Manufacturing Company (DAMCO Inc.) and Plastic Molding Manufacturing Inc. to serve Massachusetts' emerging high-tech industries. The company began as a contract manufacturer for plastic injection molding and printed circuit board assembly.

Today the company operates four plants across Connecticut, Massachusetts, Indiana, and Pennsylvania, running more than 100 injection molding presses. Its capabilities span insert molding, two-shot molding, medical-grade production in an ISO 8 clean room, scientific molding, design-for-manufacturing support, precision tooling, and a range of secondary services. The operation handles everything from rapid prototyping and low-volume runs to high-cavitation, high-volume production.

The customer base spans consumer, medical, industrial, defense, transportation, connector, and railroad sectors. The company has managed thousands of projects since its founding, producing components such as housings, industrial parts, and high-volume disposable products.

Plastic Molding Manufacturing emphasizes a 'Speed, Quality, Cost' philosophy and a long-standing commitment to re-shoring U.S. production. Differentiators cited include end-to-end in-house expertise, continuous investment in advanced molding equipment and smart-process engineering, rigorous quality management with onsite mold maintenance, and tool-transfer protocols designed to minimize downtime during supplier transitions.

name: Plastic Recycling Of Iowa Falls Inc
old_description: Manufacturing quality plastic products while protecting the environment
about:
Plastic Recycling of Iowa Falls, Inc. operates from Iowa Falls, Iowa. The business traces its roots to 1986 when Hammer's Plastic Recycling began processing mixed plastic and manufacturing products from commingled material. In 1984, Hammer's had formed Plastic Recycling, Inc. to design and build a production facility for recycling mixed-plastic waste. The company won the Iowa Governor's Award in 1988. New management took over in 1997, and the name changed to Plastic Recycling of Iowa Falls in 1999.

The company manufactures a range of recycled-plastic products including park benches, picnic tables, planters, trash receptacles, traffic safety items such as car stops and speed bumps, landscape timbers, posts, dimensional lumber, and custom-molded parts. Production runs on automated lines for large-profile items, supported by patented equipment that enables custom molding with low-cost mold design. The firm's unique molds and processes are protected by multiple U.S. and international patents.

Customers include the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, the National Park system, state and city governments, and industrial manufacturers. Washington State Parks has installed over 2,000 picnic tables; Marshall Engines uses recycled-plastic skids for shipping remanufactured engines; the Smithsonian Institution relied on the lumber for supporting a historic bell; and the City of Norwalk Parks and Recreation purchased hex tables for its aquatic center.

The company was founded to address the landfill crisis by turning plastic waste into a community resource. It emphasizes a minimum 96% recycled content (by weight) with additives limited to 4%, UV stabilizers molded in, and products that require no painting, staining, or sealing and resist warping, splintering, and rot.

about:
Plasticare, Inc. was founded in 1989 in Englewood, Colorado, and has served the Rocky Mountain region and clients across the United States for over three decades. The company operates as a fabricator and supplier of plastic and composite materials.

The shop provides custom plastic fabrication services including CNC routing, laser cutting, engraving, UV printing, saw cutting, and box fabrication. It also stocks a range of materials such as acrylic, polycarbonate, fiberglass, carbon fiber, composite resins, epoxy resins, gels, coatings, and corrugated plastic in sheet, rod, tube, and film forms. Technical consultation is offered to help customers select materials and processes.

Plasticare works with engineers, designers, creators, and fabricators across various sectors; testimonials reference event planners and individual customers needing custom-cut parts for signage, displays, enclosures, and other applications. The company ships finished components and raw materials nationwide from its Colorado facility.

The company states its mission is to empower engineers, designers, creators, and fabricators by delivering materials, precise fabrication, and technical insight, emphasizing that plastics and composites are solutions rather than substitutes. It highlights a blend of technical expertise and hands-on craftsmanship as its differentiating approach.

name: Plastilite Corporation
old_description: Developing thermally protective packaging solutions since 1958.
about:
Plastilite Corporation was founded in 1958 in Omaha, Nebraska. The company began as a manufacturer of expanded polystyrene products and has since expanded into cold-chain packaging solutions.

Today Plastilite produces EPS molded foam products including custom-molded trays, coolers, and insulated packaging under its IntegriTemp brand. The company recycles 100 percent of its scrap EPS foam during manufacturing and offers REfoam+, a recyclable and biodegradable foam made with 30 percent post-consumer recycled content. It also holds an exclusive NFL license for branded EPS coolers sold through grocery, convenience, and general retailers. Operations are based in the Midwest, allowing quick and cost-effective service.

The company serves healthcare, food distribution, and retail sectors, along with industrial manufacturers needing protective packaging for heavy parts, electronics, glass bottles, and ceramics. Its IntegriTemp line provides design, advice, and testing for temperature-sensitive shipments.

Plastilite emphasizes environmental responsibility through its closed-loop recycling program, which includes a 24/7 community drop-off for used EPS foam and a national directory of recycling centers. The NFL partnership and IntegriTemp's testing capabilities are cited as key differentiators.

name: Plastimold Products
old_description: ., As a plastic part manufacturer Plastimold specializes in mid and high volume injection molding manufacturing of small and mid sized parts.
about:
Plastimold Products operates from a 33,000-square-foot facility in Delray Beach, Florida. The company was founded in 1999 when Joe Parisi Sr., an optical-industry veteran, purchased a small injection molding shop in Fort Lauderdale. After moves to Boca Raton (2003) and Delray Beach (2007), the business remains family-owned and is now led by second-generation owners Joe and Anthony Parisi.

The shop provides custom plastic injection molding and precision CNC machining under one roof. Its 32 all-electric presses range from 45 to 390 tons with shot sizes up to 52 ounces, supporting scientific molding, overmolding, insert molding, and in-house toolmaking. CNC capabilities include 5-axis and mill/turn machining on Makino, Okuma, Mazak, and Haas machines for aerospace alloys, medical components, and mold tooling. The company handles prototype through full-scale production, with a focus on mid-to-high volumes and short runs of 1,000–10,000 parts. Assembly services such as adhesive bonding, ultrasonic welding, and fulfillment round out the offering.

Plastimold serves OEMs in aerospace, medical, defense, firearms, consumer goods, and industrial markets. Programs often involve tight-tolerance components in high-temperature polymers (PEEK, Ultem, Delrin) and structural resins, with full traceability required by AS9100, ISO 13485, and ITAR regulations.

The company emphasizes single-source responsibility—molding, machining, tooling, and inspection stay in the same plant to shorten communication loops and maintain consistent run-to-run quality. Family ownership keeps engineering leadership close to the floor, and a gated DFM-to-delivery process aims to deliver audit-ready traceability on every shipment.

name: PlumtroniX, LLC
old_description: PlumtroniX is a faith based, family-owned electronic manufacturing services company formed in 2010, later purchasing the assets of Complete Inc. in 2016.
about:
PlumtroniX, LLC, a faith-based, family-owned electronic manufacturing services provider, was established in 2010 in Springdale, Arkansas. The company expanded its capabilities in 2016 by acquiring the assets of Complete Inc., a move that broadened its assembly and integration offerings.

The company specializes in low- to medium-volume, high-mix printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) and electro-mechanical assembly. Its process portfolio includes surface-mount technology (SMT) with placement capability from 01005 components up to 55 mm packages, through-hole assembly using wave, selective, and hand soldering, and full electro-mechanical integration including wire harness and cable assembly. PlumtroniX also provides conformal coating (acrylic, silicone, urethane) and potting (epoxy, silicone) services, along with design support such as PCB layout in Altium Designer, design for manufacturability, component engineering, test development, device programming, and documentation. Product development services for microcontroller-based designs round out the offering.

PlumtroniX serves original equipment manufacturers and other businesses requiring outsourced electronics assembly, though the company does not publicly list specific industry verticals or named customers.

The firm emphasizes a quality culture built on process development, with each unit undergoing functional testing and visual inspection to IPC-A-610 workmanship standards. Customer support is highlighted as a differentiator, with staff available 24/7 to respond to requests.

name: Polar Semiconductor LLC
old_description: Polar is a 100% U.S.-based manufacturer of differentiated power and sensor technologies. Ready to embrace the future of technology?
about:
Polar Semiconductor operates from Bloomington, Minnesota, in the Upper Midwest region. The company draws on over six decades of integrated circuit and power semiconductor experience, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed. It is a 100% U.S.-based manufacturer focused on differentiated power and sensor technologies.

As a pure-play silicon foundry, Polar offers capabilities spanning gallium nitride (GaN), MOSFET, IGBT, and BCD technologies. It provides both commercial and automotive manufacturing flows, allowing customers to meet diverse product needs within a single foundry. The facility handles complex, custom orders with tailored support for clients of varying sizes.

The foundry serves the automotive, AI infrastructure (including AI data centers), aerospace and defense, and industrial markets. Global companies partner with Polar to deploy innovative power and sensor solutions while maintaining control over quality and intellectual property.

Polar emphasizes its role as a collaborative partner that secures supply chains and protects intellectual property. Its flexibility and specialized pure-play model enable it to work closely with customers on custom, high-complexity semiconductor projects.
